evidence.note: Distinguished the two deliverables by difficulty: recognized y2kr-SC could be satisfied by copying the provided perfect alignment (NC=1.0) while DM-HS needed a real algorithm — genuine effort-budgeting across deliverables.
Laid out an ordered pipeline (load → similarity → greedy seed → hill-climb) and held S3>=0.32 explicitly as the numeric done-criterion for DM-HS.
Built the scorer before optimizing, measured a baseline (S3=0.0098), and tracked measured scores against the threshold across iterations — sensible sequencing with done-checks.

Second half devolved into an undifferentiated terminal-recovery loop with no milestone tracking; decomposition structure was not sustained, though the cause was a stuck terminal rather than a planning failure.

reasoning: The agent clearly separated parsing, scoring, and alignment generation, tracked both deliverables distinctly with their thresholds as goals (meeting the level-5 anchor), and went beyond it: it built the scorer before optimizing, measured a baseline, gated on measured S3 against the numeric target, and budgeted effort by difficulty (trivially solving the yeast task via the perfect alignment while concentrating optimization on the fly task) — hallmarks of the level-8/10 anchors. It falls short of 10 because the milestone hierarchy was never crisply/formally maintained and fallback branches were only informally sketched, so I place it at 7.
